Outlet: CNBC, published Friday Nov 6 2026, 4:22 PM EST
Stock Market News for Nov. 6, 2026

The Nasdaq Composite rebounded 1.09% to close at 24,579.42. The S&P 500 rose 0.31% to 7,376.86, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 237.33 points, or 0.46%, settling at 51,285.73.

Jobs Report Beats Expectations: The U.S. economy added 165,000 jobs in October, significantly exceeding economist expectations of 59,000. The unemployment rate decreased to 4.1% from the anticipated 4.2%.

Tech Recovery After Losses: Following Thursday's severe selloff that sent the Nasdaq into correction territory with a 5.5% decline, chip stocks rebounded Friday. Advanced Micro Devices surged 9%, Intel gained nearly 7%, Qualcomm and Micron Technology each rose over 5%, and Nvidia advanced more than 4%.

Stuart Clark, portfolio manager at Quilter: "The scale of the falls in some of the market's biggest names has been striking. But it also highlights the concentration risk that has built up in U.S. equity markets."

Chris Grisanti of MAI Capital Management: "While there's definitely more of a headwind now after the election, this is an industrial revolution akin to railroads, akin to internet, and it's not going to stop."

Democratic victories sparked concerns about potential data center restrictions. Texas Governor-Elect Gina Hinojosa (CNN interview): "We need to stop what we are doing with data centers until we have those protections."
President Trump on Truth Social: "They are GOLD, and only foolish leadership will say 'NO' to the riches they bring!"

Corporate: Moderna rallied nearly 10% after beating earnings and raising full-year guidance to 15-25% revenue growth; Lam Research surged nearly 11% following a $25 billion stock buyback authorization; IonQ rose 17% after raising full-year revenue guidance to $505-$515 million; Firefly Aerospace jumped nearly 30% on a $1.3 billion agreement with AST SpaceMobile; Microchip Technology tumbled 14% on disappointing guidance.

Weekly Performance: All three major averages posted losses for the week. The Nasdaq fell 3.4%, the S&P 500 dropped 2.7%, and the Dow slid 0.9%. Thursday's deep sell-off erased $3 trillion in market value, centred on concerns about a slowdown in data center construction and in AI spending. S&P 500's worst weekly performance since June.
